- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–20% for next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ 0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; add 5–15% to forecast for next 3–7 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 2.0x recent mean), model frequently overcorrects; cap forecast at 1.5x recent peak for next 5 days.  
- If sentiment swings sharply (e.g., 0.33 → 1.00 → 0.33), model misreads momentum; apply mean reversion: forecast = 0.8×previous + 0.2×true for next 3 days.  
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overestimates early in the forecast window (days 1–7); apply linear decay: forecast[i] = forecast[i] × (1 - 0.05×i) for i=1 to 7.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 or -0.33, model underperforms; increase forecast by 10–20% for next 5 days to compensate for low sentiment bias.
